req.title: Basic-auth accepts correct credentials
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> with HTTP 200 and an authenticated=true JSON body when the supplied Basic credentials match.

doc.reasoning: The requirement covers GET /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> returning HTTP 200 with {authenticated: true, user: <user>} when correct Basic credentials are supplied. I design: (1) a positive EP test with matching credentials, (2) a negative NEG test with wrong password, (3) a negative NEG test with no credentials, (4) a DT test covering wrong username, (5) a BVA test with single-character credentials at the minimal boundary, (6) a DT test verifying the exact JSON body fields and values to catch boolean/string mutations, (7) a NEG test verifying the 401 WWW-Authenticate header is present on failure. Each test uses in-process Flask test client, exact-value assertions, and covers both sides of the boolean check in check_basic_auth.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Client sends GET /basic-auth/testuser/testpass with Authorization: Basic base64(testuser:testpass)
actions: Build Basic auth header with correct user and password
expected: Response JSON body has authenticated == True
trace: R-HTTPBIN-018: correct credentials -> HTTP 200 + {authenticated: true, user: <user>}
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'testuser:testpass').decode('ascii')
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/testuser/testpass', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == 'testuser'

test_basic_auth_correct_credentials_returns_200()

import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_wrong_password_returns_401():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'testuser:WRONGPASS').decode('ascii')
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/testuser/testpass', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 401
    body = r.data
    assert b'"authenticated": true' not in body
    assert b'"authenticated":true' not in body

test_basic_auth_wrong_password_returns_401()

tests.name: test_basic_auth_response_body_exact_fields
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Client sends correct credentials for user 'alice' and password 'secret'
actions: Build Basic auth header for alice:secret
expected: JSON body contains exactly authenticated=True (boolean, not string)
JSON body contains exactly user='alice' (not 'user' or any other string)
No extra unexpected keys that would indicate wrong routing
trace: R-HTTPBIN-018: exact body shape {authenticated: true, user: <user>}; catches mutations to boolean value or user field value
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

def test_basic_auth_response_body_exact_fields():
    client = app.test_client()
    creds = base64.b64encode(b'alice:secret').decode('ascii')
    headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/alice/secret', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] is True
    assert data['authenticated'] != False
    assert data['user'] == 'alice'
    assert data['user'] != 'passwd'
    assert data['user'] != 'user'
    assert 'authenticated' in data
    assert 'user' in data

test_basic_auth_response_body_exact_fields()

tests.name: test_basic_auth_correct_user_reflected_in_body
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Client sends correct credentials for a different user 'bob' and password 'hunter2'
actions: Build Basic auth header for bob:hunter2
expected: Response JSON user field equals 'bob', not 'alice' or any hardcoded value
